title: Art therapy for the most violent men in Scotland’s prisons
description: In 1973 the Special Unit at Barlinnie Prison, Glasgow’s Victorian jail in Riddrie, began giving violent long-term prisoners art materials and a say in their own regime. Its best-known inmate, gangster Jimmy Boyle, left as a sculptor.

title: Shipyard workers refuse to let their yards close
description: In 1971 the government let Upper Clyde Shipbuilders fail. Led by shop stewards Jimmy Reid and Jimmy Airlie, workers kept building ships instead of striking. One of the yards was Fairfield in Govan, whose 1890s offices still face Govan Road.

title: Tanks in the city after a riot in the main square
episode: Versus History #92 - Battle of George Square 1919.
spotify: Versus History Podcast Versus History #92 - Battle of George Square 1919.
description: Versus History talks to writer Donny O’Rourke about 31 January 1919, when police charged strikers campaigning for a 40-hour week in George Square, Glasgow’s civic square. The government sent troops, and tanks waited in the cattle market.

title: The art school that burned twice
episode: Rediscovering Mackintosh: A Decade After the Glasgow School of Art Fire, with Dr Robyne Calvert
place: Glasgow School of Art, Mackintosh Building
spotify: If Glasgow’s Walls Could Talk Rediscovering Mackintosh: A Decade After the Glasgow School of Art Fire, with Dr Robyne Calvert
description: Cultural historian Robyne Calvert on architect Charles Rennie Mackintosh and his Glasgow School of Art on Renfrew Street, finished in 1909 and gutted by fires in 2014 and 2018.

title: The wife Mackintosh said was three-quarters of his work
show: Love Scotland: Stories of Scotland's History and Nature
episode: The story of Margaret Macdonald Mackintosh, and why the wife of architect Charles Rennie Mackintosh deserves equal recognition
place: The Mackintosh House, Hunterian Art Gallery
spotify: Love Scotland: Stories of Scotland's History and Nature The story of Margaret Macdonald Mackintosh, and why the wife of architect Charles Rennie Mackintosh deserves equal recognition
description: The National Trust for Scotland’s podcast on artist Margaret Macdonald Mackintosh, wife and collaborator of Charles Rennie Mackintosh. The Hunterian Art Gallery at the University of Glasgow has rebuilt the interiors of the couple’s home.

title: A dance hall built by a market queen
spotify: Music Maps Podcast Glasgow Barrowlands with Alison Irvine
description: Writer Alison Irvine on the Barrowland Ballroom on the Gallowgate, opened on Christmas Eve 1934 by market trader Maggie McIver as an East End dance hall. Its neon sign and sprung floor later made it one of Britain’s best-loved rock venues.

title: How Glasgow taught the world to pass
spotify: Football Travel by Outside Write Glasgow's Early Football History
description: Richard McBrearty of the Scottish Football Museum at Hampden Park, Scotland’s national stadium, on early Glasgow football: Queen’s Park, the amateur club that pioneered the passing game, and the Irish community clubs that followed.

title: Photographing the slums before the demolition crews
episode: BoW Bites Episode 7: Thomas Annan and the Old Closes of Glasgow
spotify: Body of Work Heritage Podcast BoW Bites Episode 7: Thomas Annan and the Old Closes of Glasgow
description: Glasgow’s Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons on photographer Thomas Annan, hired in 1868 to record the closes, narrow alleys off the Saltmarket and High Street, before the city cleared them: some of the first photographs of slum housing.

title: A modernist world’s fair in a south side park
episode: May 5th, 1938 - The Empire Exhibition in Bellahouston Park, Glasgow
spotify: This Day in Scottish History May 5th, 1938 - The Empire Exhibition in Bellahouston Park, Glasgow
description: This Day in Scottish History recalls the 1938 Empire Exhibition in Bellahouston Park, south of the Clyde, which drew nearly 13 million visitors to its modernist pavilions and 300-foot Tait Tower. The Palace of Art is one of the few buildings left.

title: The novelist who painted the city’s ceilings
episode: Alasdair Gray's Glasgow with Sorcha Dallas (The Alasdair Gray Archive)
spotify: If Glasgow’s Walls Could Talk Alasdair Gray's Glasgow with Sorcha Dallas (The Alasdair Gray Archive)
description: Sorcha Dallas, custodian of the Alasdair Gray Archive, on the Glasgow writer and artist behind the novel Lanark. His murals are all over the city; the largest is the starry ceiling of Òran Mór, a former church turned arts venue on Byres Road.

title: A ship launched with its builders aboard
episode: The Clyde’s Forgotten Tragedy - The SS Daphne
spotify: Scottish History Out of Order The Clyde’s Forgotten Tragedy - The SS Daphne
description: In July 1883 the steamer Daphne capsized moments after launch at Alexander Stephen’s Linthouse yard on the Clyde, drowning 124 of the shipyard workers still aboard. Scottish History Out of Order visits their graves in Craigton Cemetery.

title: The speech the New York Times compared to Gettysburg
episode: A rat race is for rats! — Kenny MacAskill MP on Jimmy Reid's Inaugural Address as Rector of Glasgow University, 1972
spotify: Speakola A rat race is for rats! — Kenny MacAskill MP on Jimmy Reid's Inaugural Address as Rector of Glasgow University, 1972
description: Former Scottish justice secretary Kenny MacAskill on “A rat race is for rats”, the 1972 address by shipyard union leader Jimmy Reid on becoming rector of the University of Glasgow. The New York Times printed it in full.

title: From the Gorbals to guarding Abraham Lincoln
episode: #43 From the Gorbals to America's most famous private detective
spotify: Glasgow Crime Stories #43 From the Gorbals to America's most famous private detective
description: Actor Alex Norton narrates the story of Allan Pinkerton, born in 1819 in the Gorbals, the old tenement district south of the river, who emigrated to the US, foiled a plot against Abraham Lincoln and founded the Pinkerton detective agency.

title: Hundreds of children hunt a vampire in a graveyard
episode: The Iron Man of Gorbals (The Gorbals Vampire)
spotify: The Hebejeebies Podcast The Iron Man of Gorbals (The Gorbals Vampire)
description: One night in 1954 hundreds of Gorbals children armed with knives and stakes stormed the Southern Necropolis, a Victorian cemetery, hunting an iron-toothed vampire. The Hebejeebies podcast asks how the rumour started and who got blamed.

title: Suffragette bodyguards against the Glasgow police
episode: Deeds Not Words - Suffragettes & Suffrajitsu In Glasgow
spotify: Scottish History Out of Order Deeds Not Words - Suffragettes & Suffrajitsu In Glasgow
description: In March 1914 police stormed the stage at St Andrew’s Halls to arrest suffragette leader Emmeline Pankhurst, and her jiu-jitsu-trained bodyguard fought back. Only the halls’ facade survived a 1962 fire; the Mitchell Library now fills it.

title: The restaurant that claims chicken tikka masala
episode: Shish Mahal Glasgow Podcast | History, Success & Chicken Tikka Masala Origins
spotify: The Judge Reviews Shish Mahal Glasgow Podcast | History, Success & Chicken Tikka Masala Origins
description: The Judge Reviews talks to Asif of the Shish Mahal, the West End curry house whose founder Ali Ahmed Aslam said he invented chicken tikka masala there around 1971 by adding a tomato sauce to dry tandoori chicken for a customer.
